title: You prayed for the blessing…
paragraphs:
You prayed for the blessing…
but you’re breaking in the process.

And now you’re wondering—
Did God forget me?
You don’t say it out loud.

That quiet disappointment.
That hidden shame.
That silent question:
“Lord… why does obedience feel like loss?”
Because nobody told you this part.

The nights where you obey—but nothing changes.
The prayers where heaven feels silent.
The moments you choose righteousness… and it costs you everything.
You thought following God would lift you.
Confronting the parts of you you tried to hide.

You didn’t just want God’s will—
you wanted control.

You didn’t just pray for purpose—
you wanted comfort.

You didn’t just ask for blessing—
you expected it on your terms.
Just not the way your flesh imagined.
Here’s the truth most people won’t say:
Preparation feels like humiliation before it feels like elevation.
But first, he was betrayed by his own brothers.
But then ran for his life in caves, hunted like prey.
Lived in obscurity, rejected, and crucified.
“After you have suffered a little while, He will restore you, confirm you, strengthen you, and establish you.” — 1 Peter 5:10
Some scholars interpret this “suffering” not just as external trials, but the internal breaking of pride, self-reliance, and false identity.
God isn’t just changing your situation.
And that’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because God will answer your prayer—

By confronting the version of you
that can’t carry what you asked for.
He will deal with your insecurity.
He will uncover your hidden sin.

God doesn’t anoint what you pretend to be.
He redeems who you’re willing to surrender.
And this is where Jesus steps in.
Because the real problem isn’t just your situation.
Sin that makes us want control instead of surrender.
Sin that chooses self over God.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
Jesus didn’t wait for you to fix yourself.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
The cross was not just suffering.
So you could receive what you never earned.
God is not trying to destroy you.

From the version of you
that would sabotage the very thing you prayed for.
So what do you do now?
Because the same God who is breaking you…

You are not being delayed.
You are being developed.
Bring the real you to Jesus.
Trust in Him—not just for blessing—
Because the greatest thing God is preparing you for…

“Lord, I surrender.
Not just my dreams—but my heart.
Break what needs to be broken.
Heal what needs to be healed.
Forgive my sin, cleanse me, and make me new through Jesus.
I trust Your process.
I trust Your cross.
Amen.”
